ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $ \triangle ABC$, extend $ BC$ to point D such that $ CD=AB$, draw $ DE\parallel AB$ with $ DE=BC$, and connect $ CE, AE$. $ \angle BAC=\angle DCE$; If $ \angle B=32^\circ$ and $ \angle ACD=58^\circ$, what is the measure of $ \angle CEA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle B=32^\circ$ and $\angle ACD=58^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DCE=\angle BAC=\angle ACD-\angle B=58^\circ-32^\circ=26^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ACE=\angle ACD+\angle DCE=58^\circ+26^\circ=84^\circ$,\\
since $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle CDE$,\\
it implies $AC=CE$,\\
thus, $\angle CEA=\angle CAE=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-\angle ACE\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-84^\circ\right)=\boxed{48^\circ}$.

Reasoning: Because CD is an extension of BC, ∠ACD is the exterior angle at point C of triangle ABC, therefore ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠B. It is known that ∠ACD = 58°, ∠B = 32°, so ∠BAC = 58° - 32° = 26°. It is also known that ∠BAC = ∠DCE, therefore ∠DCE = 26°. Thus ∠ACE = ∠ACD + ∠DCE = 58° + 26° = 84°.

Then compare triangle ABC and triangle CDE: It is known that AB = CD, BC = DE; and because B, C, and D are collinear and DE ∥ AB, the included angle ∠ABC = ∠CDE can be obtained. Therefore △ABC ≅ △CDE (SAS), so AC = CE.

In triangle ACE, AC = CE, so the base angles ∠CAE = ∠CEA. Also ∠ACE = 84°, therefore ∠CEA = (180° - 84°) / 2 = 48°.

推理链符合题意、图像和标准答案。候选先描述图像再推理，满足多模态顺序要求；图像描述中 B、C、D 共线且 C 在中间，A 在上方、E 在下方，已连接相关线段且 DE 与 AB 平行，均与图像一致。角追踪、余弦定理证明 AC=CE、最终得到 48° 的过程也与方法草稿一致。无需实质修改。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, extend $BC$ to point $D$ such that $CD=AB$, draw $DE\parallel AB$ with $DE=BC$, and connect $CE$ and $AE$. Given $\angle BAC=\angle DCE$, $\angle B=32^\circ$, and $\angle ACD=58^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CEA$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Since $\angle B=32^\circ$ and $\angle ACD=58^\circ$, it follows that $\angle DCE=\angle BAC=\angle ACD-\angle B=58^\circ-32^\circ=26^\circ$. Therefore, $\angle ACE=\angle ACD+\angle DCE=58^\circ+26^\circ=84^\circ$. Since $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle CDE$, it implies $AC=CE$. Thus, $\angle CEA=\angle CAE=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle ACE)=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-84^\circ)=\boxed{48^\circ}$.
